
`lode rule supersede --map <file> [--dry-run]` (`POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/rules/supersede`) applies a map of old rules to their successors in one transaction. Each line is `OLD -> NEW [NEW ...]`, or `OLD ->` to withdraw with no successor, and a line starting with `#` is a comment. A ref is a rule ref or a `<doc>#sec-N` ref, resolved to the rule at that anchor, and may name another project's rule. Every ref is resolved and validated before the first write, and one bad line refuses the whole map: an unparseable ref, an old rule listed twice, a successor that is withdrawn or also on the left side, or a ref that names no rule. Every rule on the left side becomes `withdrawn`, each successor gets a `supersedes` edge to it with source `refactor`, and every accepted plan with a `covers` edge to a rule the map withdraws is marked `stale`. The whole map is one `rule.superseded` event. Re-running an applied map changes nothing and reports zero counts. `--dry-run` resolves the map and reports the counts (rules withdrawn, edges written, tasks told, plans marked stale) without writing. A task governed by a withdrawn rule keeps its link and is never rewritten by the refactor (WL-SPEC-77#sec-4bb).
